name: Lemongrass

schedule.notes: Easiest from a rooted grocery-store stalk in water for 3 weeks. Buy a plant in cold-summer regions.
Cut whole stalks at the base. Plant must be well-established (at least 12 stalks) before first harvest.

harvest.cues: Stalks 1/2 to 3/4 in thick at the base; tough outer leaves and fragrant fleshy inner stem.
harvest.storageNotes: Fresh in fridge 2 weeks. Freeze whole stalks; flavor holds well. Dried tea leaves keep a year.

varieties.name: East Indian (West Indian) Lemongrass
varieties.notes: Cymbopogon citratus, the cooking lemongrass. Used in Thai and Vietnamese dishes.

notes: Below zone 9 grow as an annual or overwinter indoors in a pot. Single stalks become huge clumps (3 ft wide, 4 to 5 ft tall) by season's end. Roots easily from a fresh grocery-store stalk in a glass of water.
